{{short description|American statistician}}
'''Ji-Hyun Lee''' is an American statistician whose research involves [[clinical trial]]s, especially for the [[treatment of cancer]].{{r|more}}

Lee did her graduate studies in [[biostatistics]] at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]], where she earned a master's degree in 2000 and completed her doctorate in 2003. She joined the faculty at the [[University of South Florida]] in 2003, and in 2014 moved to the [[University of New Mexico]] as a professor of internal medicine and director of biostatistics in the UNM Comprehensive Cancer Center. Since 2018 she has been a professor of biostatistics at the [[University of Florida]] and director of biostatistics and quantitative sciences in the University of Florida Health Cancer Center.{{r|cv}}

Lee was president of the [[Caucus for Women in Statistics]] for the 2017 term,{{r|cws}} and in 2018 was elected as a [[Fellow of the American Statistical Association]].{{r|fasa}} She was elected as [[List of presidents of the American Statistical Association|the 120th President of the American Statistical Association]] who serves in the year of 2025.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ji-Hyun Lee Elected 2025 ASA President and Susan Paddock Elected Vice President {{!}} Amstat News |url=https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2023/07/01/2025pres/ |access-date=20 July 2024 |work=AMSTAT News |date=1 July 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230703124732/https://magazine.amstat.org/blog/2023/07/01/2025pres/|archive-date=3 July 2023}}</ref>
